messages:
jia: Kicking off apac-west1 cluster bootstrap now. terraform apply started, will validate networking + gpu pool. tagging @kevin and @sam for handoff.
kevin: ack. i'll watch the tf plan bits and the IAM roles. last time we had a race on instance profile attach.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: terraform apply returned non-zero exit code 1 at step 'aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.attach'. error: "EntityAlreadyExists: RolePolicy with same name exists"
jia: ugh, looks like leftover role from test run. i tried a quick `aws iam list-role-policies --role-name redwood-apac-west1-node` and it's showing the policy.
kevin: can we rm the old policy and re-run? or better, import the existing resource into the tfstate so we don't delete/create in prod.
sam: +1 import is safer. command we'd run locally: `terraform import aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.node_attach redwood-apac-west1-node:policy/NodeDefault`
oliver: heads up — while debugging IAM i noticed some pods in the new nodepool fail kubelet cni init due to MTU mismatch. logs: `failed to set interface mtu: invalid argument: requested 9000 but max 1500`
maria: that would break gpu drivers attaching PVs. did we set an MTU override in the VPC module? i remember apac regions default to 1500 on the cloud provider side.
jia: checking our templates: network module has `mtu = var.mtu_override` but default is null. looks like the boot script for the image set 9000 in userdata. bad combo.
kevin: ok stop the rollout on the rest of the nodegroups. @jia can you patch boot scripts to use 1500 for apac-west1 and rebootstrap one test node?
jia: will do. also found a related issue: gpu driver DaemonSet crashed with `kernel module version mismatch` on the AMI we selected (custom-ami-gpu-2025-11). stacktrace snippet: ```stderr: modprobe: FATAL: Module nvidia not found in directory /lib/modules/5.10.0-xyz```
sam: oh that explains some of the boot failures we saw earlier. driver <-> kernel mismatch. we should switch to official gpu ami or rebuild. what's the cost/time tradeoff?
oliver: rebuilding AMI will take ~3hrs, switching to official ami is faster but we lose our custom telemetry hooks. we can push telemetry as a DaemonSet instead.
maria: for handoff: propose 1) revert nodegroup autoscaling to 0, 2) import IAM artifacts into tfstate, 3) patch userdata mtu->1500, 4) switch AMI to official-gpu-2026-01 then re-run bootstrap on one node. if green, escalate to full roll.
kevin: agree. also add a tfguard check to prevent role/policy recreate on existing role names. we'll add a preflight `aws iam get-role` check in the runbook.
jia: i'm going to run the import + patch on a dry-run workspace now, will report back.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: workspace 'apac-west1-bootstrap' status: running (operator=jia). planned actions: import(1), taint(0), apply(1).
kevin: ping if you need infra-oncall to temporarily hold traffic or flip DNS.
sam: note for cost — we already have one reserved GPU in staging for testing; if we rebuild AMIs and keep staging running, cost bump ~ $1.2k/day. keep finance in loop.
maria: thanks — i'll open a short incident doc and tag finance. minimal next steps: import IAM, patch mtu, switch AMI, validate node becomes Ready, verify GPU drivers load `nvidia-smi` output, then handoff to platform for full rollout.
jia: update — imported role into tfstate, patched userdata mtu to 1500, kicked off a single-node apply. waiting for node to reach Ready. will post logs.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: apply completed with exit code 0. new node ip=10.12.4.21, instance id i-0abc123def.
jia: node reached Ready, gpu daemonset now reports `nvidia-smi` present. running a few sample inference jobs to validate perf.
kevin: great. assemble a short checklist for handoff: list import commands used, AMI id chosen, mtus, and the tf guard PR link.
maria: I'll take the handoff once tests finish. thanks everyone for quick turnaround :thumbsup:
